evidence: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: createApp(service: FulfilmentService) sends every route through service methods (listProducts, getProduct, addProduct, placeOrder, listOrders, getOrder, transition, cancelOrder).
src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: the GET /orders state filter uses the domain's isOrderState instead of its own copy of the state list, and the error handler maps DomainError.kind through STATUS.

src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProductRepository implements ProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository. Both are pure storage adapters with no business rules.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: the composition root builds FulfilmentService from the in-memory repositories, seeds data through service.addProduct, and calls createApp(service).listen.
Minor: http-app.ts builds the product shape {id, name, stock} three times (GET /products, GET /products/:id, POST /products). This is local duplication, not a duplicated invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The infrastructure module holds one concern: the adapters and composition root that connect the application core to concrete technology. http-app.ts is the HTTP adapter and talks only to FulfilmentService. in-memory-repositories.ts implements the application's ProductRepository and OrderRepository ports. server.ts wires the two together and starts the server. The HTTP adapter goes through the service's methods throughout, so it never bypasses the module's abstractions or reaches into repositories directly. Domain rules are reused rather than copied: order-state validity comes from isOrderState in the domain, and error kinds come from DomainError. The request-shape checks in the POST handlers only validate incoming JSON, which is the adapter's job; they don't duplicate business invariants. One minor issue: http-app.ts builds the product response shape {id, name, stock} three times. That is a small local duplication inside one file, not a rule or invariant scattered across the module, so it does not reach the fail threshold.
